# Proj4 parity fixtures

Reference: proj4js **2.22.0**, tag **v2.22.0**, checked September 28, 2026.

- `parity-inventory.json` inventories all 38 upstream projection/helper files, their
  aliases/default-bundle inclusion, and 30 input/API/transformation features. A partial
  status means numerical support for the documented subset, with unresolved CRS or
  parameter gaps. Unsupported rows have a named gap and target tranche. Explicitly
  out-of-scope APIs are those math.gl does not expose, such as MGRS and mutable globals.
- `common-projections.ts` contains authored cases used for independent forward,
  inverse, and round-trip comparisons. Each case is exercised in meters, US survey
  feet, and kilometers. Forward tolerance is 1e-5 meters (3e-5 feet), inverse comparison
  tolerance 1e-8 degrees, and round trips 1e-7 degrees. Kilometer cases use 1e-5 output
  units; the meter run provides the stricter physical accuracy check.
- `upstream-2.22.0.ts` adapts 24 PROJ-string fixtures from
  [the tagged upstream test file](https://github.com/proj4js/proj4js/blob/v2.22.0/test/testData.js).
  Original definitions and coordinates are retained with line numbers and a SHA-256
  of the original source file. Twenty-two cases execute numerically; two retain
  explicit datum/ellipsoid rejection expectations for future tranches. Their rounded
  expected coordinates use 0.02 meter / 2e-6 degree tolerances. Inverse longitude is
  compared modulo 360 degrees. Upstream attribution is in `../../PROJ4-LICENSE.md`.
- Published [PROJ UTM examples](https://proj.org/en/stable/operations/projections/utm.html)
  provide independent north/south checks at their published 0.01-meter precision.
  They use default GRS80; its difference from WGS84 is below this precision. These are
  published examples, not outputs generated by a local PROJ installation. A larger
  independently generated native corpus remains an explicit inventory gap.

Run `node modules/proj4/scripts/check-parity-inventory.mjs` from the repository root
to validate the reference version, source hashes, inventory completeness, and fixture,
test, and gap links. It reads the installed pinned upstream package and needs no
network. Run the proj4 Vitest suites to exercise numeric fixtures in Node or Chromium.

To update the baseline, change the exact upstream dependency, review release notes,
refresh the module/alias inventory and source hashes from that tag, import new
fixtures with attribution, and rerun both checks. Do not overwrite expectations with
the new native implementation's own outputs. Recent upstream fixes in not-yet-ported
algorithms stay listed as gaps until their fixtures can execute.
